target_persona: VP Marketing / Growth, Docs leader, or Product Operations

evidence.fact: Sentry maintains a substantial public documentation codebase using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind and MDX; the repository showed more than 18,000 commits when researched.
The docs repository visibly contains AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, a .claude directory and Cursor rules, providing public evidence of agent-oriented development workflows.
Sentry's agent instructions define AI-oriented contribution workflows, including brand-guideline, docs-review and technical-docs skills.
Sentry's main repository documents pull-request and CI guardrails, including sequencing requirements when changes span frontend and backend.
The public docs repository has a high-volume pull-request history, supporting the view that reviewable GitHub changes are a normal operating mechanism.

hypotheses.statement: A plausible Sparkles wedge is enabling marketing, docs or operations teammates to request bounded code/content changes while preserving Sentry's existing PR, CI and review controls.
The likely objection is not 'AI is too new' but 'we already have strong AI coding workflows'; Sparkles would need to prove differentiated value for non-engineering teammates and governance.

unknowns: Whether Sentry currently has a material backlog of non-engineering requests waiting on engineers.
Whether non-engineering teammates already use an internal agent workflow directly against production repositories.
Who owns the relevant cross-functional workflow and budget.
Current employee count and engineering-team size were intentionally left unset rather than inferred.
